title: Earthquake Safety
description: Essential steps to protect yourself during and after an earthquake

steps.title: Drop, Cover, and Hold On
steps.description: Immediately drop to your hands and knees, take cover under a sturdy desk or table, and hold on to it. If no table is available, cover your head and neck with your arms.

steps.title: Stay Where You Are
steps.description: If indoors, stay indoors. If outdoors, stay outdoors. Do not run outside during shaking as most injuries occur when people try to move during an earthquake.

steps.title: Avoid Dangerous Areas
steps.description: Stay away from windows, mirrors, hanging objects, tall furniture, and exterior walls that could fall or shatter.

steps.title: If in a Vehicle
steps.description: Pull over safely, stop the vehicle, and stay inside. Avoid overpasses, bridges, and power lines. Once shaking stops, proceed cautiously.

steps.title: After Shaking Stops
steps.description: Check for injuries and hazards. Be prepared for aftershocks. Turn on a battery-powered radio for emergency information.

steps.title: Evacuate if Necessary
steps.description: If your building is damaged, evacuate carefully. Use stairs, not elevators. Watch for falling debris and broken glass.

title: Fire Emergency
description: Critical actions to take when facing a fire emergency

steps.title: Alert Everyone
steps.description: Immediately alert all occupants by shouting 'Fire!' and activate the fire alarm if available.

steps.title: Call Emergency Services
steps.description: Call 911 immediately. Provide your exact location, nature of emergency, and any people trapped.

steps.title: Evacuate Immediately
steps.description: Leave the building immediately using the nearest safe exit. Do not use elevators. Stay low if there's smoke.

steps.title: Check Doors Before Opening
steps.description: Feel doors with the back of your hand before opening. If hot, use an alternate route. If cool, open slowly and be ready to close quickly.

steps.title: Stay Low in Smoke
steps.description: Crawl under smoke to the nearest exit. Smoke rises, so cleaner air is near the floor.

steps.title: Meet at Assembly Point
steps.description: Once outside, go to the designated meeting point and stay there. Do not re-enter the building for any reason.

title: Flood Safety
description: Protective measures for flood situations and water emergencies

steps.title: Move to Higher Ground
steps.description: Immediately move to the highest floor of your building or to higher ground. Avoid basements and ground floors if flooding is imminent.

steps.title: Avoid Walking in Water
steps.description: Never walk through flowing water. Six inches of moving water can knock you down. Use a stick to check depth if you must walk.

steps.title: Don't Drive Through Floods
steps.description: Turn around and find an alternate route. Just 12 inches of rushing water can carry away a vehicle. Remember: 'Turn Around, Don't Drown.'

steps.title: Disconnect Utilities
steps.description: If time permits and it's safe, turn off utilities at main switches. Do not touch electrical equipment if you're wet or standing in water.

steps.title: Gather Emergency Supplies
steps.description: Collect drinking water, non-perishable food, flashlight, battery-powered radio, first aid kit, and medications.

steps.title: Listen for Updates
steps.description: Monitor local emergency broadcasts for evacuation orders and safety information. Follow all official instructions.

title: Severe Weather Safety
description: Protection strategies for storms, tornadoes, and severe weather events

steps.title: Monitor Weather Alerts
steps.description: Stay informed through weather radio, TV, or mobile alerts. Understand the difference between watches and warnings.

steps.title: Seek Appropriate Shelter
steps.description: For tornadoes: Go to the lowest floor, center of building, away from windows. For lightning: Stay indoors, avoid water and metal objects.

steps.title: Avoid Windows and Doors
steps.description: Stay away from windows, skylights, and glass doors. Flying debris is the greatest danger in severe weather.

steps.title: Have Emergency Kit Ready
steps.description: Keep emergency supplies accessible: water, food, flashlight, radio, batteries, first aid kit, and medications.

steps.title: Stay Connected
steps.description: Keep mobile devices charged. Have backup power sources. Identify multiple ways to receive emergency information.

steps.title: Wait for All Clear
steps.description: Don't venture outside until authorities confirm it's safe. Be aware of downed power lines, debris, and flooding.

title: Medical Emergency Response
description: First aid and emergency medical response procedures

steps.title: Assess the Situation
steps.description: Check for responsiveness. Tap shoulders and shout 'Are you okay?' Look for signs of breathing and consciousness.

steps.title: Call for Help
steps.description: Call 911 immediately. Provide clear location, nature of emergency, number of victims, and your contact information.

steps.title: Check ABCs
steps.description: Airway: Ensure airway is clear. Breathing: Look, listen, feel for breathing. Circulation: Check for pulse and severe bleeding.

steps.title: Control Bleeding
steps.description: Apply direct pressure to wounds with clean cloth. Elevate injured area above heart level if possible. Don't remove embedded objects.

steps.title: Monitor Vital Signs
steps.description: Keep checking breathing and pulse. Be prepared to perform CPR if trained. Keep victim warm and comfortable.

steps.title: Provide Information to EMS
steps.description: When emergency services arrive, provide all relevant information about the incident and any care you've provided.

title: Power Outage Preparedness
description: Steps to stay safe and comfortable during extended power outages

steps.title: Check Circuit Breakers
steps.description: First, check if the outage is just in your home by checking circuit breakers and fuses. Look outside to see if neighbors have power.

steps.title: Report the Outage
steps.description: Contact your utility company to report the outage. Use their mobile app or website if available, or call their emergency number.

steps.title: Use Flashlights Only
steps.description: Never use candles, gas lanterns, or camp stoves indoors. Use battery-powered flashlights and lanterns for lighting.

steps.title: Preserve Food Safety
steps.description: Keep refrigerator and freezer doors closed. Food will stay cold for 4 hours in refrigerator, 24-48 hours in full freezer.

steps.title: Stay Warm or Cool
steps.description: Dress in layers for warmth. Close off unneeded rooms. Never use generators, grills, or camp stoves indoors due to carbon monoxide risk.

steps.title: Conserve Phone Battery
steps.description: Use phones sparingly to preserve battery. Turn on low power mode. Have backup power sources like power banks charged.

title: Home Security Emergency
description: Actions to take when home security is compromised

steps.title: Ensure Personal Safety
steps.description: If you suspect an intruder, do not confront them. Hide in a secure room with a locked door, or leave the premises immediately if safe to do so.

steps.title: Call Emergency Services
steps.description: Call 911 immediately. Speak quietly if hiding. Provide your address, situation details, and stay on the line as instructed.

steps.title: Secure Yourself
steps.description: If hiding, lock the door, turn off lights, silence your phone, and stay away from windows. Have an escape route planned.

steps.title: Don't Investigate
steps.description: Never go to investigate suspicious sounds or check on the source of alarm activation. Wait for law enforcement to arrive.

steps.title: Identify Yourself to Police
steps.description: When police arrive, clearly identify yourself. Keep hands visible. Follow all instructions carefully.

steps.title: Document and Report
steps.description: After the situation is resolved, document any damage or theft. File a police report and contact your insurance company.

title: Chemical Spill Response
description: Safety procedures for hazardous chemical exposure or spills

steps.title: Evacuate the Area
steps.description: Immediately leave the area of the spill. Move upwind and uphill if outdoors. Alert others to evacuate as well.

steps.title: Call Emergency Services
steps.description: Call 911 and report the chemical spill. Provide the chemical name if known, location, and extent of contamination.

steps.title: Remove Contaminated Clothing
steps.description: If chemicals contacted your clothing or skin, remove clothing immediately and rinse affected areas with water for 15-20 minutes.

steps.title: Avoid Contact
steps.description: Do not touch spilled chemicals. Avoid walking through contaminated areas. Keep others away from the spill zone.

steps.title: Seek Medical Attention
steps.description: If exposed to chemicals, seek immediate medical attention even if you feel fine. Bring the Safety Data Sheet if available.

steps.title: Follow Decontamination
steps.description: Follow instructions from emergency responders for decontamination procedures. Do not re-enter the area until cleared by authorities.

title: Gas Leak Emergency
description: Critical safety steps for natural gas or propane leaks

steps.title: Don't Ignite Anything
steps.description: Do not light matches, lighters, candles, or cigarettes. Do not turn electrical switches on or off, including light switches.

steps.title: Evacuate Immediately
steps.description: Leave the area immediately. Do not use phones or electrical devices inside the building. Get to fresh air.

steps.title: Shut Off Gas if Safe
steps.description: If you can safely reach the gas meter outside, turn off the main gas valve. Use a wrench to turn the valve a quarter turn.

steps.title: Call From Safe Distance
steps.description: Once you're at a safe distance, call 911 and your gas company. Do not re-enter until authorities say it's safe.

steps.title: Open Windows and Doors
steps.description: If safely possible before evacuating, open windows and doors to ventilate the area and help disperse the gas.

steps.title: Stay Away
steps.description: Do not return to the building until emergency responders and gas company personnel declare it safe.

title: Winter Storm Preparedness
description: Essential preparation for blizzards and severe winter weather

steps.title: Stock Emergency Supplies
steps.description: Gather water (1 gallon per person per day for 3 days), non-perishable food, medications, flashlights, batteries, and first aid kit.

steps.title: Prepare Heating Sources
steps.description: Check heating system, stock up on fuel if using wood/coal. Have extra blankets available. Never use generators or grills indoors.

steps.title: Protect Pipes
steps.description: Insulate pipes, disconnect garden hoses, and know how to shut off water. Let faucets drip slightly to prevent freezing.

steps.title: Prepare Vehicles
steps.description: Fill gas tanks, check antifreeze, battery, and tires. Keep emergency kit in car: blankets, food, water, tools, and medications.

steps.title: Stay Informed
steps.description: Monitor weather forecasts and warnings. Have battery-powered or hand-crank radio for updates if power goes out.

steps.title: Avoid Travel
steps.description: Stay indoors during storms. If you must drive, inform someone of your route and expected arrival time. Keep car kit stocked.
